explicit_validation.explanation: Paper explicitly compares Gemini-as-a-judge results with human evaluation results through Pearson correlation analysis reported in tables, showing quantitative metrics of agreement.

prompts.notes: Prompt was in the same format as given to human annotators; exact prompt template shown in annotation interface examples in Appendix A.3

guidelines.notes: Detailed annotation protocol described including 1-4 Likert scale, corruption strategies, and qualification questions; UI interface shown in Appendix A.3 with examples

sample_size.notes: 400 samples per language across 8 languages; all samples evaluated by both Gemini-as-a-judge and human annotators

quantitative_scores.notes: Gemini-as-a-judge exhibited the lowest correlations among neural metrics regardless of language resource level

correlation_interpretation.threshold_used: Not explicitly stated, but results show Gemini-as-a-judge performs worse than other neural metrics

validation_results.summary_finding: Gemini-as-a-judge exhibited the lowest correlations with human scores among all neural metrics evaluated, indicating that LLM-as-a-judge methods still lag behind other automated evaluation approaches in aligning with human judgments.

criteria_mapping.notes: Both LLM-as-a-judge and human evaluation used identical evaluation criteria (coherence and completeness) on the same set of summaries
